grooveshop.name: GrooveShop E-commerce
grooveshop.description: A multi-tenant e-commerce platform built over four years: every store gets its own database schema behind one Django REST API, with a Nuxt storefront, a NestJS media service and a Go agent gateway that makes each store shoppable by AI agents over MCP. Promotions, gift cards, loyalty and B2B pricing are built in.

webside.title: Webside.gr, a store in production
webside.summary: Webside is a Greek store for phone and computer accessories that runs on GrooveShop, the platform I build. I write the software and operate everything under it, from the Kubernetes cluster to the release pipeline.
webside.stack: Nuxt · Django · NestJS · Go · PostgreSQL · Redis · Meilisearch · RabbitMQ · Celery · k3s · Argo CD · Longhorn · Cloudflare · Grafana · VictoriaMetrics

store.title: The store
store.body: Webside sells phone and computer accessories, with a Greek-language tech blog alongside the catalogue. It started taking real orders in May 2026, and September and October have been its busiest months so far.

platform.title: One tenant of the platform
platform.body: Since August 2026 Webside is one store on the multi-tenant GrooveShop platform: its own PostgreSQL schema, domain, theme and credentials, served by the same API, storefront and workers as every other store. Its data moved with it, order history and uploaded media included.

operations.title: Running it
operations.body:
Everything runs on a self-hosted k3s cluster at Hetzner that I set up and operate. Argo CD deploys from Git. Before a release goes live, a pre-sync job checks the migrations are safe, migrates every store, collects static files and applies the search index settings. After it, post-sync jobs purge the Cloudflare edge cache and warm the storefront.

Longhorn provides the volumes, Cert-Manager renews TLS, Sealed Secrets keeps credentials encrypted in Git, and VictoriaMetrics with Grafana tracks the cluster and alerts when something drifts, while VictoriaLogs keeps the logs.

ekfyseosfyteias.title: Ek fyseos Fytias, a cooperative's site on the platform
ekfyseosfyteias.summary: A women's social cooperative in Fytia, Imathia makes jams, spoon sweets and trachanas. I replaced its two broken sites with one on GrooveShop: a Greek and English site with the cooperative's own design, domain and blog, and a shop that can be switched on later.
ekfyseosfyteias.stack: Nuxt · Django · django-tenants · PostgreSQL · Redis · k3s · Argo CD · Cloudflare

site.title: The site
site.body: A home page, a page for the products, the cooperative's story, a page for its funding programme, a blog and a contact page with a map and opening hours. It publishes LocalBusiness structured data with the hours and the location. There is no checkout yet: the catalogue is empty and every payment method is off, so the site presents the products and orders still go by phone.

platform.title: One more tenant
platform.body: It is a store on the multi-tenant platform, with its own PostgreSQL schema, domain and theme, served by the same API, storefront and workers as the others. Its pages are built from a kit of sections (media with text, features grid, gallery, opening hours, map) that I added to the platform for it and that every other store can now use. The look is its own: a sage and mint palette with a terracotta accent, set in Commissioner and Vollkorn.

move.title: The move
move.body:
The old site was a NuxtHub deployment that returned errors, next to an older site on shared hosting that did the same. I imported its 13 blog posts from WordPress with their images, translated them into English, rewrote the legal pages from what the site actually does, and moved everything to its own domain.

Each data script is idempotent and runs in one database transaction, so a failed run changes nothing and a re-run is safe.

grooveshop.title: GrooveShop, a multi-tenant commerce platform
grooveshop.summary: GrooveShop is the e-commerce platform I've been building for more than four years. One deployment runs many stores: each gets its own database schema, domain, theme, and payment and courier credentials, and turns features such as loyalty, gift cards or B2B on and off.
grooveshop.stack: Django · DRF · django-tenants · Channels · Nuxt · NestJS · Go · PostgreSQL · Redis · Meilisearch · RabbitMQ · Celery

platform.title: One platform, many stores
platform.body: A request's host name selects the store's own PostgreSQL schema, so stores share code and infrastructure but never data. A control plane provisions stores, bills them and suspends them, and every release migrates all of them in one tenant-aware step before it goes live. Four stores run on it today, the demo among them.

commerce.title: Commerce, built in
commerce.body: A rule-based promotion engine with coupons and automatic discounts, stored-value gift cards with a ledger, loyalty points with tiers, and a wholesale programme with VIES VAT validation and group pricing. Payments go through Viva Wallet or Stripe, or cash on delivery; shipping through ACS and BoxNow. Search is Meilisearch with Greeklish transliteration, so a Greek product is found when typed in Latin letters, and order updates reach the browser over WebSockets.

agents.title: Shoppable by AI agents
agents.body: A Go gateway makes every store usable by AI agents: an MCP server with commerce tools for search, cart, checkout and order tracking, UCP and ACP endpoints for agentic checkout, product feeds for Google Merchant, Meta and TikTok, and the backend of the storefront's own shopping chatbot.

services.title: The services
services.body: A Django REST API holds the business logic and data. The Nuxt storefront renders on the server, and its Nitro layer validates every request with Zod before proxying it to Django. A NestJS service resizes and serves images, the Go gateway serves agents, and a documentation site covers both the admin panel and the internals.
